bio: Town at the Bellarine Peninsula's tip, home to Fort Queenscliff and the terminus of the Bellarine Railway.
1860 fort guarding the entrance to Port Phillip, entered by weekend guided tour only; bring ID.
Volunteer-run steam railway from Queenscliff along 16 km of former branch line towards Drysdale.
Torquay museum with the Australian Surfing Hall of Fame and boards from early wooden designs to modern ones.
Aireys Inlet lighthouse, the 'White Lady' of Round the Twist, with a climb to the top for 360-degree coastal views.
gaps: Children 5 and over only; weather permitting.

bio: Bass Strait town 21 km south of Geelong, gateway to the Great Ocean Road and home of the national surfing museum.
Timber-log arch over the Great Ocean Road at Eastern View, honouring the returned servicemen who built the road.
gaps: Current arch build date unresolved (sources conflict), so left out.

bio: A 35.5 m single-drop waterfall in the Otways 10 km inland from Lorne, with a lookout and about 240 steps to the base.
gaps: Lower steps reportedly closed at times; check Parks Victoria.

bio: A 15.8 m waterfall on Sheoak Creek beside the Great Ocean Road in Great Otway National Park, about 6 km from Lorne.
Great Ocean Road settlement between Lorne and Apollo Bay, where wild koalas live in the gums along Grey River Road.
gaps: Koala sightings not guaranteed; unmade road.

bio: Victoria's oldest working lighthouse on Cape Otway, a heritage precinct with whale watching in winter and spring.
gaps: Tower climbs closed for conservation works; bio avoids promising the climb.

bio: An 800 m self-guided circuit walk through cool temperate rainforest in Great Otway National Park near Apollo Bay.
An 18 m single-drop waterfall on the Aire River in Great Otway National Park, reached by a 1 km return walk.
A 1.8 km walk through ancient rainforest to a platform viewing three cascades, past an old timber mill site.
An 18.7 m single-drop waterfall near Beech Forest in the Otways, reached by a walk of about 3 km return.
A 600 m steel Treetop Walk 25 to 30 m above the Otway forest floor, with a 47 m Spiral Tower and guided ziplines.
Limestone gorge with a sheltered beach, where two of the 54 people aboard the 1878 Loch Ard wreck survived.
Quartz sand that squeaks underfoot, between granite boulders near Tidal River; unpatrolled, with strong currents.
Natural rock window framing the coastline on the Shipwreck Coast, just beyond Port Campbell near London Bridge.
gaps: The Arch viewing area next door is closed; not mentioned.

bio: Sea cliffs and rock stacks near Peterborough, quieter than the big stops, with whales offshore May to October.
Great Ocean Road town west of the Twelve Apostles, base for the Shipwreck Coast sights and whale spotting in season.
Maritime museum and village on Flagstaff Hill in Warrnambool, alongside the original lighthouses and garrison.
Geothermal bathing sanctuary in Warrnambool with an indoor bath house, outdoor pools and two-hour sessions.
Wildlife reserve in a dormant volcano crater 15 km north-west of Warrnambool, with emus, koalas and walking trails.
